scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window due to travel.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Minh Nguyen and I'm 75. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Nguyen. I understand how frustrating it is to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your service subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8829-4401 and the email is m.nguyen@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security purposes, could you please confirm your billing zip code and the last four digits of the payment method used for this service?
The zip code is 90210 and the card ends in 4492.

Thank you, Mr. Nguyen. I have verified your account. I see the cancellation was processed 34 days ago. While our 'Standard Subscription Refund Policy' (KB-992) strictly limits automated refunds to 30 days, I have reviewed your account history and see you have been a loyal customer for five years with no prior billing disputes. Given these circumstances, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to the policy.
Oh, that would be wonderful. Thank you so much for understanding.

It is my pleasure to help. I have successfully processed a full refund of $49.99 to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit reflect on your statement within 3-5 business days depending on your financial institution. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and utilized discretionary authority to override the 30-day refund policy (KB-992) due to the customer's long-standing tenure and positive account history.
